title: Finite-ring chart adjunction on the finite-Tor categories
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On either the ordinary etale or pro-etale site let $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T,R)$ mean the full category of constant-$R$ module complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The finite Tate line is $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ on the etale site and its comparison inverse image on the pro-etale site; $(d)$ denotes tensor with its $d$th tensor power [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].
Let $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ be separated etale of finite type and put $g=p_de$. Choose compactifications with standing middle schemes [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $R=A,B$ set $H^{et}_{g,R}=e_R^*p_{d,R}^*(-)(d)[2d]$, and let $F^{et}_{g,R}$ and $F^{pro}_{g,R}$ be the chosen compact-support candidates [def-amb-etale-compact-support, det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Give $F^{et}_{g,R}\dashv H^{et}_{g,R}$ the adjunction obtained from $De_{\Sigma!,R}\dashv e_R^*$ and the ordered affine-space adjunction by the graph-normalized left comparison [def-sp-etale-adjoint-chart-comparison, lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Both functors restrict to $\mathcal C_{-,R}$. The exact comparison $C_{T,R}=\nu_T^*$ is an equivalence between the etale and pro-etale finite-Tor categories [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback, det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. For a quasi-inverse $Q_{Y,R}$, the functor $C_{U,R}H^{et}_{g,R}Q_{Y,R}$ is right adjoint to $F^{pro}_{g,R}$ and is canonically the geometric functor $H^{pro}_{g,R}=e_R^*p_{d,R}^*(-)(d)[2d]$. On $C_{Y,R}K$, its counit is
$$\widetilde\epsilon_{g,R,C_{Y,R}K}=C_{Y,R}(\epsilon^{et}_{g,R,K})\circ c_{g,R}(H^{et}_{g,R}K)^{-1},$$
with the canonical endpoint identifications; $c_{g,R}:C_{Y,R}F^{et}_{g,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{pro}_{g,R}C_{U,R}$ is the fixed proper-and-open comparison [def-sp-fixed-compact-support-comparison]. There is a unique counit-preserving natural isomorphism $\theta_R:H^{pro}_{g,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}g_R^!$, where $g_R^!$ is the constructible Brown right adjoint [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation].

proof.text: Every standing scheme is Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, and finite type over a Noetherian scheme preserves Noetherianness [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Also $N=\ell^n$ is invertible on every standing scheme because $\ell\ne p$; both coefficient rings are finite Noetherian rings since an ascending chain of subsets of a finite set stabilizes. Apply [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain] to $h=g$ and separately to $R=A,B$. It supplies preservation of $\mathcal C$ by $F^{et}_{g,R}$ and by $e_R^*p_{d,R}^*(-)(d)[2d]$. Apply [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] on $U,Y$: the same fixed Tor interval is preserved and reflected, and $C_{U,R},C_{Y,R}$ are equivalences on these full subcategories.

For one fixed $R$, let $E_R=De_{\Sigma!,R}$, let $F_{d,R}$ be the ordered affine-space left functor, and set $G_{d,R}=p_{d,R}^*(-)(d)[2d]$. The exact sum adjunction $E_R\dashv e_R^*$ is given by [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]; [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] gives $F_{d,R}\dashv G_{d,R}$, including the identity adjunction when $d=0$. Compose their Hom bijections as in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The right functor is $e_R^*G_{d,R}=H^{et}_{g,R}$, and the composite counit is $\epsilon_{d,R}\circ F_{d,R}(\epsilon_{e,R}G_{d,R})$: evaluation over the etale sheets followed by the ordered affine-space counit.

By [lem-sp-chart-left-scalar-normalization], the specified graph-normalized left comparison $\lambda_R:F_{d,R}E_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{et}_{g,R}$ carries precisely this composite adjunction to the chosen compact-support functor, through the canonical refinement to the chosen compactification. Concretely its counit at $K$ is the Step 2 composite counit precomposed by $\lambda_R(H^{et}_{g,R}K)^{-1}$. Since Step 1 places both functors in the full finite-Tor subcategories, their ordinary Hom bijection restricts unchanged to those subcategories. This proves the specified $F^{et}_{g,R}\dashv H^{et}_{g,R}$ on $\mathcal C_{-,R}$.

source.place: Charts: normalized left comparison, retained Step 11

proof.text: For the fixed compactification of $g$, [lem-sp-finite-compact-support-domains] says that the map obtained from the proper counit mate and open comparison is invertible on every bounded-below etale input. By [def-sp-fixed-compact-support-comparison] its inverse is the displayed comparison with orientation $F^{pro}_{g,R}C_{U,R}\simeq C_{Y,R}F^{et}_{g,R}$, so the forward map is exactly the fixed $c_{g,R}$ in the item. Step 1 ensures the needed bounded-below inputs. Essential surjectivity of $C_{U,R}$ now also proves that $F^{pro}_{g,R}$ preserves $\mathcal C$: write an input as $C_{U,R}M$, apply $c_{g,R}^{-1}$, and use $C_{Y,R}F^{et}_{g,R}M\in\mathcal C$.

source.place: Charts: actual fixed proper-and-open comparison, retained Steps 3--4 and 11

proof.text:
Apply [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer] with $f=g$, $G=H^{et}_{g,R}$, and the very comparison $c_{g,R}$ verified in Step 4. This gives $\widehat H_R=C_{U,R}H^{et}_{g,R}Q_{Y,R}$ as a right adjoint of $F^{pro}_{g,R}$. Explicitly, for $M\in\mathcal C_{U,R}^{et}$ and $K\in\mathcal C_{Y,R}^{et}$ its Hom bijection is
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C_UM,C_UH^{et}_{g,R}K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,H^{et}_{g,R}K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F^{et}_{g,R}M,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(C_YF^{et}_{g,R}M,C_YK)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F^{pro}_{g,R}C_UM,C_YK).$$
The last arrow precomposes by $c_{g,R}(M)^{-1}$. Taking $M=H^{et}_{g,R}K$ and the identity of $C_UH^{et}_{g,R}K$ gives exactly $C_Y(\epsilon^{et}_{g,R,K})\circ c_{g,R}(H^{et}_{g,R}K)^{-1}$, with the equivalence endpoint identifications. Fullness and essential surjectivity give the bijections for arbitrary objects and their naturality, as asserted by the transfer lemma.

source.place: Charts: transported adjunction and its actual counit, retained Step 4

proof.text:
The canonical comparison isomorphisms in [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain] intertwine site comparison with scheme inverse image, finite Tate powers and shifts. Thus
$$C_{U,R}H^{et}_{g,R}K\simeq e_{pro,R}^*p_{d,pro,R}^*C_{Y,R}K(d)[2d]=H^{pro}_{g,R}C_{Y,R}K.$$
Here the pro-etale Tate line is defined to be the comparison inverse image of the etale line, so no comparison with a different coefficient convention is required. Evaluating this natural isomorphism at $Q_{Y,R}L$ and then using $C_{Y,R}Q_{Y,R}L\simeq L$ identifies $\widehat H_RL$ canonically with $H^{pro}_{g,R}L$. It preserves $\mathcal C$ by Step 1. Carrying the adjunction along this isomorphism gives the counit of Step 5 at $C_{Y,R}K$ under exactly these endpoint identifications.

source.place: Charts: geometric identification of the transported right functor, retained Steps 3--4

proof.text: By [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] the Brown adjunction for this separated finite-type $g$ restricts to $F^{pro}_{g,R}\dashv g_R^!$ on the same constant-ring finite-Tor categories. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to this adjunction and the one from Steps 5--6. Its isomorphism $\theta_R:H^{pro}_{g,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}g_R^!$ is the unique transpose of $\widetilde\epsilon_{g,R}$; equivalently $\epsilon^{Brown}_{g,R}\circ F^{pro}_{g,R}(\theta_R)=\widetilde\epsilon_{g,R}$. The reverse transpose is its inverse. This proves existence, naturality and counit-preserving uniqueness for each $R=A,B$.

tool_uses.why: Noetherianness of the standing schemes is a generic finite-type permanence tool.
The precise finite-Tor site equivalence is a generic comparison tool, not another geometric purity route.
Exact etale sum extension supplies the elementary chart factor adjunction.
The ordered affine-space adjunction is the affine factor required by the unit route.
The definition fixes the sum-then-affine composite counit.
The fixed proper/open site map is invertible on bounded-below inputs; the unit has no replacement for this comparison theorem.
Generic transfer along the finite-Tor site equivalences supplies the actual transported counit.
The constructible Brown adjunction is the second right adjoint on the same full categories.
Generic counit-preserving uniqueness identifies the two specified right adjoints.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NW-92f67ca85 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS on content: this split has no new nodes and keeps the item statement unchanged. Each of the seven steps checked against what its cited nodes actually state. Step 1: the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma, the chart-domain lemma (preservation of D^b_ctf by F^et_g and g^*(-)(d)[2d]) and the finite-Tor comparison (equivalences C_U, C_Y). Step 2: u_!⊣u^* plus the ordered affine-space adjunction, composed with counit ε_d∘F_d(ε_e G_d), which matches def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction. Step 3: the chart-left normalization statement explicitly carries this composite adjunction to F_g. Step 4: compact-support-domains gives invertibility of the proper-mate/open map on D^+, and the fixed comparison def is its inverse, so c_{g,R} has the item's orientation; pro-étale preservation follows by essential surjectivity. Step 5: all hypotheses of the adjunction-transfer theorem are checked, its counit formula is the item's verbatim, and the Hom chain is correct. Step 6 is correctly marked elementary: it substitutes the chart-domain intertwining isomorphisms, with the pro-étale Tate line defined as ν^* of the étale line. Step 7: the Brown adjunction restricts to D_ctf for an arbitrary field and arbitrary finite ℓ-primary A, and det-sp-unique-right-adjoint gives θ_R. Rf_! of sk-prop-sf-existence is Rp_*D(j_!) for the chosen compactification, the same functor as F^pro. Edge cases checked: d=0, empty U, the zero ring, and non-flat Z/ℓ²→Z/ℓ. No cycle, no SGA citation, no repair note. Blueprint source checked: the Charts paragraph of sk-lem-sp-reduction-exceptional.proof.md (lines 20-36); the item covers exactly parent Step 4's use. Batch-5 check: the cite of lem-sp-finite-compact-support-domains reaches lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison. That node is a general module-object/ringed-topos derived comparison, not a step of the Poincaré duality or trace formula proofs. A recomputed closure of the two batch-5 targets, with and without the new citation, has 17942 nodes both ways (difference 0): both nodes were already in the closure. Accepted.
